cards.name: Sonar ping (spent)
cards.flag: dead: never-ping bot wins 49.4% of games vs full bot

ambiguities: Mine when the sub holds only Sonars/no salvage: loses nothing, steps still cancelled (rules say so; interpreted as written).

Ping when the trailer also has the choice: the rival 'plots first, alone' but the rival has no way to know a ping is coming (the ping is announced in phase 1, so the rival can adapt: interpreted as announced).
Mid-round Mine and own torpedo: a cancelled T step does not fire (interpreted from 'cancelled steps have no effect'); rules mention it only for moves.
Torpedo steals 'highest-value' card from a pile that holds only a card the thief just took that step (simultaneous entry + fire): resolved in order enter then fire, as written.
Ping reveal order for step 1-2 cards: a revealed card that is later blocked still stays locked (assumed).
Round-12 end with salvage still on the grid: the 12-round cap is not a bug but 71% of games end here; no rule says what happens if neither player can reach any salvage.

problems.problem: Runaway leader rate got worse, not better
problems.evidence: 0.831 (strategic pairings) vs 0.795 previously, target <= 0.65; strategic mirror 0.78, mid-v-mid 0.78, greedy mirror 0.79, random mirror 0.76: every pairing is 0.76-0.92. Mirrored zoned deal barely moved it (v1 single-shuffle deal 0.794 vs v2 0.78 in S-v-S). Lead changes 1.50 vs 1.5 previously (target 2).
problems.fix: Structural: the game is a race to a finite pile of points with no catch-up that triggers on score gaps. Candidate levers: make a hit/steal bigger than the pile gap (steal 2 cards), a leader-only penalty (leader on a Mine loses highest card), or end the game on a shared pile so scores keep moving. Do not rely on the Sonar.

problems.evidence: Never-ping bot wins 49.4% vs full strategic (must be <= 45%); with a 3-step reveal 52%. Pings 0.35 per player per game; ping spent has negative win correlation (-0.17, it is only available to the trailer).
problems.fix: Cut Sonar (replace by Salvage 1 or a Mine), or give the ping an effect a bot can use for guaranteed gain (e.g. the pinger also sees the rival 3rd card AND the rival cannot torpedo that round).

problems.problem: Coasting: 71% of strategic games end on the round-12 cap; late rounds are empty
problems.evidence: In the narrated game P1 sat at 7-15 for the last 3 rounds with no route to salvage. Length 11.0 rounds (est 17.1 min at 85 s/round vs 15 target, +14%, inside +-20% but the per-round time is a guess).
problems.fix: Cap at 9-10 rounds or end the game when the gap exceeds remaining salvage value.

problems.problem: Round 1 is mostly a home-waters race, with a quarter of games having a first-round collision
problems.evidence: Round-1 collision in 41.5% of strategic games; the leader after round 1 wins 58.2% (down from coin-flip-like deal luck but still a +8 over fair). In the narrated game both subs went home and never met until R3.
problems.fix: None required for round 1 itself; the 3-point wrecks in row 3 did not pull subs together early enough.

problems.problem: Reading layer is real but moderate; torpedo and middle are healthy
problems.evidence: Cooling-blind bot wins 41.4% (<=45 pass, previous reading value ~5 pts). No-torpedo bot 29.9%, no-middle bot 29.2%, camper 48.8% (<=55 pass), spammer 48.4% vs strategic (no exploit). Strategic v mid 50.8%: mid (K=2) is as good as strategic (K=6) so lookahead depth beyond 2 plans adds nothing.
problems.fix: None; note greedy -> mid is the real skill step (77.7%).

turn_cap_note: no games failed to end; 71% of strategic-bot games (58% mirror) end on the round-12 cap with salvage left on the grid
